# Cross-circuit geometry and a quantitative integer-slack obstruction

This note uses the full common-contact inequalities of
`candidate d2b290ebd8e35052`. It proves a simultaneous
two-circuit normal form in one integer coordinate, then gives an exact
four-circuit family showing that a defect depending only on small
integer witness gaps cannot repair the previously false basin-volume
promotion. The auxiliary contacts in the counterexample are outside
C. No claim about contacts of the exact Tukey region is refuted.

## 1. A simultaneous two-contact normal form when n=1

Suppose there are two cap groups with attained common contacts
`q_0=(r_0,y_0)`, `q_1=(r_1,y_1)`, where `r_0<r_1`. Every cap margin
is nonpositive at both contacts, and all margins in group i vanish
at q_i. In each group the continuous normals have a positive circuit.

There is ONE lattice-preserving fiber shear, shared by the groups,
after which every left-group margin has the form

    u_0j dot x+c_j(r_0-z),  c_j>=0,

and every right-group margin has the form

    u_1j dot x+b_j(z-r_1),  b_j>=0.                     (1)

The signs in (1) hold individually for every cap, not merely after
averaging the integer coefficients with circuit weights.

To prove this, subtract from x the affine interpolation
`y_0+(z-r_0)(y_1-y_0)/(r_1-r_0)`. Both contacts then have continuous
coordinate zero. A left margin is `u dot x+v'(z-r_0)`. Its value at
the right contact is `v'(r_1-r_0)<=0`, forcing `v'<=0`. A right margin
similarly has `v'(r_0-r_1)<=0`, forcing `v'>=0`. This is an actual
fiber shear, fixes z, and preserves all cap incidences and mixed
volumes exactly.

Suppose in addition each group has full continuous rank d and its
projected coefficient is nonzero. Define the two simplices

    B_0={x:u_0j dot x<=c_j for every j},
    B_1={x:u_1j dot x<=b_j for every j}.

Each is bounded and full dimensional, and contains zero, possibly on
its boundary. Indeed the full-rank positive circuit makes the
recession cone trivial. If lambda is the positive circuit normalized
to sum one, the weighted sum C of its right sides is strictly
positive. The system `u_j dot x=right_side_j-C` is consistent because
its only compatibility relation is the lambda relation; it gives a
strictly feasible point. Thus the complementary intersection of the
two groups has real fiber

    (z-r_0) B_0 intersect (r_1-z) B_1,
                      r_0<=z<=r_1,                      (2)

and has no fiber outside that interval. At each endpoint the
corresponding zero factor means the singleton zero; this endpoint
assertion uses full rank. The weighted circuit inequalities prove
emptiness outside, and zero belongs to both scaled bodies inside.

For lower-rank circuits, the coefficient signs (1) remain valid.
At an endpoint the corresponding zero-right-side system is the
continuous-normal kernel, so it must not be replaced by a singleton.
No cap-volume inequality follows solely from this geometric normal
form without relating B_0,B_1 and their contacts to the actual fibers.

## 2. A family with vanishing own witness gaps

Retain the actual six-fiber body from
`candidate d0f838592db846be`, specified here completely.
Its integer projection is

    J={(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)}.

The affine continuous center map is

    b(z)=(11-4z_1-4z_2,4z_1-5).

At `(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)` take the translated square
`b(z)+[-1/10,1/10]^2`. At the other three points use radius `1/100`.
Let C be the convex hull of these six fibers. The five projection
vertices retain exactly their prescribed fibers. The remaining integer
point `(1,1)` already has the largest square; every convex combination
with that base has the same affine center and radius at most 1/10.
Thus the convex hull has exactly the displayed integer fibers.

It is full dimensional, all six fibers have positive area, and

    V=1/25, v=1/2500, M=3V+3v=303/2500.

The binary witnesses are denoted 00,10,01,11. Fix any
`0<epsilon<=1/100`. Define four affine functions

    ell_00(z)=-(z_1+z_2)/10+epsilon,
    ell_10(z)=(z_1-z_2)/10-1/10+epsilon,
    ell_01(z)=(z_2-z_1)/10-1/10+epsilon,
    ell_11(z)=(z_1+z_2)/10-1/5+epsilon.

In every group use the three continuous normals

    u_1=(1,0), u_2=(0,1), u_3=(-1,-1),

and the closed caps

    H_sj={u_j dot x+ell_s(z)>=0}.                         (3)

The positive circuit weights are all 1/3. Write
`ell_s=a_s dot z-h_s` and put

    beta_00=0, beta_10=beta_01=1/10, beta_11=1/5.

Then every own witness gap is exactly

    delta_s=beta_s-h_s=epsilon.                          (4)

For two distinct binary witnesses p_s,p_t, the cross-witness slack
`eta_st=beta_t-a_t dot p_s` is either 1/10 or 1/5. Consequently

    max_s delta_s / min_(s!=t) eta_st=10 epsilon ->0.      (5)

All expanded witness inequalities are strict at every other witness,
and the expanded diamond has no integer point in its interior.

## 3. All common and cross contacts persist quantitatively

The complementary auxiliary polytope has projection exactly

    10 epsilon<=z_1+z_2<=2-10 epsilon,
    |z_1-z_2|<=1-10 epsilon.                            (6)

Necessity follows by adding the three inequalities in each circuit;
sufficiency follows by taking x=0. The region is bounded. Every
integer point in it would have integer sum one, hence odd integer
difference of absolute value at least one, contradicting (6).
Therefore it is globally lattice-free.

The three continuous normals positively span R^2, so the auxiliary
body is bounded in x as well. All inequalities are strict at
`z=(1/2,1/2),x=0`, proving full dimensionality. Its four attained
contacts can be chosen as `(r_s,0)`, where

    r_00=(5 epsilon,5 epsilon),
    r_10=(1-5 epsilon,5 epsilon),
    r_01=(5 epsilon,1-5 epsilon),
    r_11=(1-5 epsilon,1-5 epsilon).

All three own-group margins vanish there. For a different group,
the margin is either `-1/10+epsilon` or `-1/5+2 epsilon`.
In particular EVERY cross-contact inequality is strict by at least
9/100, uniformly over this whole parameter range. Also

    |r_s-p_s|=5 sqrt(2) epsilon ->0.                       (7)

Thus this family retains full-rank positive circuits, bounded
full-dimensional lattice-free auxiliary bodies, all attained contacts,
uniformly strict cross-contact compatibility, and contacts whose base
coordinates approach their own integer witnesses.

## 4. The cap masses and basin defect stay fixed

For every s and every z in J,

    -3/10<ell_s(z)<=11/100.

At the three large-fiber centers the normal-sign patterns are the
three separate cap colors: `(3,-1)` is in cap 1 only, `(-1,3)` in
cap 2 only, and `(-1,-1)` in cap 3 only. The radius-1/10 squares keep
these signs strictly even after any of the displayed ell shifts.
For example an unintended coordinate cap has margin at most
`-9/10+11/100=-79/100`; an unintended third-normal cap has margin at
most `-18/10+11/100<0`. The intended margins stay strictly positive.
The other three fiber centers are `(11,-5),(7,-1),(7,-5)`; their
radius-1/100 squares are strictly in cap 1 only for all shifts above.

Therefore all four groups have, independently of epsilon, exactly

    mu(H_s1)=103/2500,
    mu(H_s2)=mu(H_s3)=100/2500.                          (8)

The expanded witness parity forest is unchanged. Its root-11 basin
is exactly `{(1,1),(2,1),(1,2)}`, of mass `3/25`, because the two
nonroots both map to `(1,1)` under coordinatewise `ceil(z/2)`.
The same group covers this entire basin for every epsilon. Yet

    gamma_2 mu(basin_11)-max_j mu(H_11,j)
       =(4/9)(3/25)-103/2500=91/7500.                   (9)

The difference is strictly positive and does not tend to zero.
All twelve caps obey, for example, the common strict budget
`T=104/2500`.

Here `D_int=[-1/5,1/5]^2`, so the continuous widths of the three
normals are `1/5,1/5,2/5`, independent of epsilon. Thus the vanishing
in (4) is not obtained by shrinking the entire cap normal. After
normalizing each continuous normal to its D_int width, the circuit
weights become `(1/4,1/4,1/2)` and all projected gaps and cross
slacks are multiplied by the same factor 15/4. The ratio (5) and
the failure (9) are unchanged.

In particular, an inequality of the form

    max_j mu(H_11,j)
      >=gamma_2 mu(basin_11)-M f(max delta/min eta)

cannot hold for all such certificates if `f(t)->0` as `t->0`.
Indeed (9) requires `f(10 epsilon)>=91/909` for every epsilon in
the displayed range. The same objection applies to an error that
vanishes with the base-contact displacement (7), while allowing only
the other uniformly controlled data exhibited here.

## 5. Scope of the obstruction

The auxiliary contacts `(r_s,0)` are not asserted to belong to C;
indeed in this body they lie outside it. Their base coordinates can
approach the correct integer witnesses while their continuous
coordinates remain far from the corresponding actual fibers. The
finite grouped certificate permits exactly this situation. Hence a
new argument using actual Tukey-region contacts in C would require
and use an additional hypothesis not refuted here.

The common cap budget above is also well above the OC target
`gamma_2 M/4`. This example disproves a proposed integer-slack repair
of the basin promotion under the full finite geometric certificate.
It does not disprove a quantitative inequality that additionally
uses the below-target budget or minimizing-body conditions, and it
does not disprove OC.
